title: KB3b: seven-source singleton f(7) continued - parity closes L=19, beating templates closed, cover/walk dichotomy, resumable 20-cycle census (no new kappa)

# KB3b: seven-source singleton `f(7)` continued — parity closes L=19, beating templates closed, cover/walk dichotomy, resumable 20-cycle census

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in scoping, implementation, verification and writing; no model named; no independent human review claimed). No kappa, supplier, certificate or selected-frontier change.

## Change and mathematical scope

In the [PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) prefix-walk model ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943), `research/universal-connector-boundary`), a restored source word `w` over seven singleton labels is universal when paired readouts realize every mask, `D(w) = {q_s xor q_t} = F2^7`, and `f(n)` is the minimum word length. The pinned record ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185), `research/universal-connector-six-source`) left `18 <= f(7) <= 24`; the predecessor of this package removed 18 ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542), `f(7) >= 20`), so the recorded gap is `20 <= f(7) <= 24` with the Gray bound 24 attained. This package (kappa-blocker KB3b, a scoped continuation) advances the next step and reports:

1. **Length 19 is closed exactly, for a structural reason.** Every restored word has even length (all label counts even and at least 2; the cube is bipartite and walks are closed), so no odd length exists to census. The assignment's literal "exclude length 19" is discharged by [PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943)'s restoration facts, and the census step-up from 18 is `L = 20`.
2. **Two natural Gray-beating templates are impossible** (proved lemmas, machine spot-checked): a single-excursion square-detour word `[6, i, j, i, j, 6]` plus a 16-cycle forces its cycle set `R` to be a transversal of the coordinate square, but a transversal's induced-cube graph has the level-set components of its offset map `g`, so a closed walk through `R` needs `g` constant — which makes `R + R` a 16-point plane and misses 48 masks. No word of that template is universal at any length.
3. **20-point covers of `F2^7` exist** (explicit verified example; set-ILS finds covers in 14 of 30 restarts at `k = 20`, 28 of 30 at `k = 22`) — answering part of the predecessor's open question 2 in the direction `r((C2)^7) <= 20`. But every cover sampled (175 at `k = 20` and 288 at `k = 22` in session sweeps, plus the deterministic campaign) has an isolated hypercube vertex, hence admits no closed walk at any length. Covers and walk-shaped sets look disjoint at `k <= 22`; this is quantified evidence, not an exclusion.
4. **A deterministic search campaign with an `L = 24` non-vacuity control** tops out at 120/128 (length 20) and 126/128 (length 22), and finds 128/128 at length 24 in the same optimizer. Extended 600-restart runs confirm both ceilings. These are search failures, not exclusions; they agree with the pinned package's heuristic record (126/128 at length 22).
5. **A resumable restricted-growth simple-20-cycle census** (the `|P| = 20`, `(10,10)` split of `L = 20`, PR 2542's proved-necessary prunes and the split-identity budget `e_ex + b_ex <= 27`) runs with exact per-shard node counts checkpointed in `CENSUS20-PROGRESS.json`. At submission 11 of 15 shards are complete: 798,901,058 nodes and 67,674,177 simple 20-cycles checked, zero universal words (the completed heavy shard `0102` alone accounts for 798,901,031 nodes and 67,674,177 cycles; the small shards die instantly on the self-avoidance prune). The three remaining heavy subtrees are of the same order — a capped probe of `0123` passes 5,000,000 nodes in 21.4 s (234,169 nodes/s) — so completing the `(10,10)` exclusion needs several more hours of the same exact enumeration; the checkpoint is resumable. No universal word appears in the 67.7 million cycles checked so far.

The gap `20 <= f(7) <= 24` is unchanged. The alphabet is singletons only; the charged DUO pair-source family ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2396](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2396), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2128](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2128), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2156](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2156)) and the 63-mask weight-1/2/3 sparse family ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2229](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2229), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2236](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2236), [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2397](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2397)) are distinct scopes, recorded as concurrent.

## Method: smallest falsifying instance first

Before any new number, the package reproduces the pinned `research/universal-connector-six-source/EXPECTED.json` byte-for-byte (histograms and records SHA-256 included): 945 words max 31/32 at `n = 5`, length 10 (`3dcc5689…`); 10,395 words max 49/64 at `n = 6`, length 12 (`491b295f…`); 945,945 words max 59/64 at `n = 6`, length 14 (`3d711ffa…`); plus the counting lower bounds 10/14/18 and the Gray constructions 12/16/24. It then fully re-runs the predecessor's decisive length-18 census against its vendored byte-pinned engine and reproduces 15,775,992 nodes, 312,064 simple 18-cycles, zero universal words. Nothing above is taken on trust.

## Reproduction and checks

From the repository root, standard library only, Python 3.12:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-l20-seed06704c39/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-l20-seed06704c39/independent.py
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-l20-seed06704c39/test_engine.py
python3 -I -B research/universal-f7-singleton-l20-seed06704c39/census20.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/universal-f7-singleton-l20-seed06704c39 --check-only
```

Observed markers:

```text
PASS_F7_L20_VERIFY <conclusion> L20=120 L22=126 seconds=...
PASS_F7_L20_INDEPENDENT {"cover20": "size=20 min_degree=0 no_closed_walk", ...}
Ran 14 tests in 0.040s — OK
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
```

`independent.py` re-checks coverage with three formulations (dual predicate, interval XOR, position pairs) and re-derives the parity fact and the covers' degree obstructions with independently written loops. `test_engine.py` pins the vendored engine byte-exactly (SHA-256 `82e4c407…`), checks the transversal level-set lemma on a deterministic sample, and confirms the deterministic set-ILS hit. The search campaign (`search.py`) is deterministic (fixed CPython `random` seeds); `search.py --extended` runs the 600-restart session budget recorded in `CERTIFICATE.json`.

## Scope and open questions

A finite study inside [PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943)'s abstract interface; no supplier instantiation and no kappa claim. Not checked: the repeated-state `L = 20` splits (`(10,9)`, `(10,8)`, `(9,9)`, `(10,7)` — note the identity kills only the 17-point splits `(9,8)`/`(8,9)`, so `|P| = 17` walks remain open), the `L = 22` census splits, and set-level exhaustive enumeration. Structured next questions are in `TASK.json` and the package README: extend the census to the repeated-state splits with per-split budgets; decide `r((C2)^7) = 20` or lower; and settle whether covers and walk-shape are incompatible at `k <= 22` (which would make the Gray bound 24 sharp).

## Credit

[PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) model and first exact values: Ross Richardson (`research/universal-connector-boundary`). Pinned five/six-source record, counting bounds and Gray constructions: Douglas Colkitt (`research/universal-connector-six-source`, [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185)). Length-18 exclusion, the restricted-growth cycle census engine (vendored here byte-exact with hash pin and credit in `NOTICE.md`/`SOURCES.json`), and the pair-representation identity: Aaron Wang with help from opencode ([https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542)). The community nine-point five-bit census fact used as a control there is published at [https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18931315](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18931315).
